verdict.rationale: Gmail's docs confirm open-protocol access: standard IMAP, POP and SMTP for non-Gmail clients, OAuth 2.0 on those servers, and syncing of messages and labels into Outlook, Apple Mail or Thunderbird. Nothing in the pack documents a first-party standards-based export format, and the API's backup and migration uses are developer building blocks that earn no credit here. Community reports also say Gmail's own export tools fail on 100GB+ inboxes and that its IMAP IDLE does not propagate read-status changes. Missing for 10: JMAP support, a documented standards-based export (e.g. mbox) with format details, export that works for large mailboxes, and a fully conformant IMAP implementation.

support.subject: As a switcher, my mail stays reachable over open protocols and standard formats — IMAP/JMAP/SMTP access and standards-based export — so no client can lock me in

citations.quote: 您可以使用标准 IMAP 和 POP 协议将第三方电子邮件客户端和应用连接到 Gmail 以接收邮件，并使用 SMTP 协议发送邮件。
The Gmail IMAP, POP, and SMTP servers support authorization with the industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol.
When you add Gmail, your messages and labels are synced with the email client.
